defects.first words of a command that opens with: a command whose first word holds an equals sign is no plain command, and the old splitter refused one read whole; asked for a command's first words it returned them before it applied that rule, so the same command was plain by its first three words and not plain whole. The new splitter applies the rule to both. The one caller that asks for first words (the near-miss advisory for a publish helper) compares the first with node's name and path, so both answers end it alike wherever node's path holds no equals sign
defects.a quote left open inside a script handed: the old splitter took the argument of eval, or of a shell's -c, as one quoted word and called the command plain; the shared reader reads the script that argument is, and a quote the script never closes makes the command no plain one, as the shell that runs it would refuse it
